lastCompletedStory.title: Isolate the three largest plan-runner test files onto a generic plan fixture

nextStoryContext:
US-007 (CAM-420) applied the audit F-03 configPath-fixture-isolation idiom to the three largest plan-phase test files (96 of the ~158 plan-phase invocations): test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner.test.ts (786 lines, 44 call sites across two builders), test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner-replan.test.ts (492 lines, 31 call sites, one builder), and test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner-container.test.ts (463 lines, 21 call sites, one builder with NO overrides parameter). plan-runner.test.ts's makeOpts (Partial<RunPlanPhaseOptions>) and plan-runner-replan.test.ts's makeReplanOpts (Partial<RunPlanPhaseWithReplanOptions>) each got their own module-level GENERIC_PLAN_CONFIG_PATH fixture (own mkdtempSync dir, `[backend]
planner = "claude"
auditor = "claude"
` project.toml -- both phases declared since these suites exercise both spawn steps -- afterAll cleanup) plus the exact loop.test.ts idiom: `configPath: 'configPath' in overrides ? overrides.configPath : GENERIC_PLAN_CONFIG_PATH,` placed AFTER the `...overrides` spread. plan-runner.test.ts's second builder, makeOptsAlwaysAlive(reportAfterTicks), has no overrides parameter; it got a literal `configPath: GENERIC_PLAN_CONFIG_PATH` sibling key directly in its returned opts object for full-file isolation (beyond what AC1's oracle strictly required, since correctness --- not just the grep --- was the goal). plan-runner-container.test.ts's makeOpts(container, spawnCalls) builder has zero 'overrides' occurrences across its 21 call sites (all built from named non-Partial parameters), so per the PRD's audit finding F-03 it got its own module-level GENERIC_PLAN_CONFIG_PATH fixture and a literal `configPath: GENERIC_PLAN_CONFIG_PATH` sibling key inside the object makeOpts returns, with its own dedicated AC2 oracle (`grep -q 'configPath: GENERIC_PLAN_CONFIG_PATH'`) rather than the overrides-idiom grep, which is structurally unsatisfiable for a builder with no overrides parameter. RunPlanPhaseOptions.configPath and RunPlanPhaseWithReplanOptions (which extends it) already existed as a DI seam from US-002 of this same PRD (CAM-420) and thread into readPhaseBackend('planner'|'auditor', configPath) / resolvePhaseModel inside plan-runner.ts, so this story was pure test-fixture wiring, zero src/ changes. All three files measured 0 process.chdir per the story notes, so no opt-out (`configPath: undefined`) call sites were needed anywhere. Verification: the three files individually run 96 pass / 0 fail (44+31+21); full `bun test` unchanged at 5633 pass / 0 fail (no tests added/removed, fixture wiring only, matching this PRD's honesty label that behavioral falsifiability for the plan side is deliberately deferred to US-010's dress rehearsal per issue AC10 -- nothing in the committed config resolves planner/auditor to codex, so these are claims about new code only); `bun run typecheck` clean; `bun run check:all` fully green after raising plan-runner-container.test.ts's file-size-budget.json ceiling to the gate-measured content.split('
').length count (464->482; the other two of the three grew but were never budgeted files, so no ceiling applied to them at all) with a dated _ref note naming this story and CAM-420, staged in the same commit. Any future story adding a NEW runPlanPhase/runPlanPhaseWithReplan call site with an inline (non-builder-routed) opts literal in any of these 3 files must add its own configPath: GENERIC_PLAN_CONFIG_PATH sibling key to keep the isolation intact. Remaining plan-phase test files outside this PRD's scope (the audit's ~158 total minus these 96) are untouched.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Pure test-fixture DI-isolation story, mirroring US-003/US-004/US-005/US-006 of this same PRD exactly: no new external library surface introduced. RunPlanPhaseOptions.configPath already existed (US-002 of this PRD) and was already wired into readPhaseBackend/resolvePhaseModel for the planner and auditor phases; this story only threaded the pre-existing seam into three plan-phase test files' builders (two via the overrides idiom, one via a literal default with no overrides parameter to hang off).
